chain.title: Charge the first crystal
chain.desc: Build a Charger and power it with a wooden crank or a compatible energy source. It can charge a compass for meteorite hunting and certus quartz for later processing.

chain.title: Find the sky-stone landing
chain.desc: Charge a compass, then follow the Meteorite Compass toward sky stone. Search the meteorite center for the mysterious cube and its processor presses.

chain.title: Inside the meteorite
chain.desc: Recover sky stone and inspect the meteorite's central cube. Keep the presses and budding certus blocks useful; destroying the wrong budding block can cost a renewable crystal source.

chain.title: Harvest certus carefully
chain.desc: Collect certus quartz from the meteorite's crystal growth. Plan a renewable supply before spending every crystal; this guide follows the 1.20.1 budding-quartz system.

chain.title: Recover the processor presses
chain.desc: Retrieve the silicon, logic, calculation, and engineering presses from the mysterious cube. The quest detects the silicon press; the other three are needed for a complete processor workshop.

chain.title: A charged ingredient
chain.desc: Charge certus quartz in the Charger. Keep some charged crystals for the fluix reaction rather than converting your entire certus supply.

chain.title: Make fluix in water
chain.desc: Drop charged certus quartz, nether quartz, and redstone together into water. Collect fluix crystals for cables, machines, and the growth accelerator.

chain.title: Set up the processor bench
chain.desc: Power an Inscriber and use the correct press for each printed circuit. The finishing step combines the printed circuit, printed silicon, and redstone.

chain.title: Prepare silicon
chain.desc: Use the installed smelting recipe for silicon, then print it with the silicon press. Processor production needs both printed silicon and a circuit-specific printed component.

chain.title: Logic for everyday devices
chain.desc: Print the gold-based logic circuit and finish a Logic Processor. These supply the first storage components and terminals, so keep a small batch ready.

chain.title: Calculation and control
chain.desc: Use certus quartz with the calculation press, then finish the processor. This branch supports crafting interfaces and network improvements.

chain.title: Engineering for larger systems
chain.desc: Print a diamond-based engineering circuit. Engineering Processors open drives, controllers, and crafting infrastructure; keep this branch separate from optional wireless features.

chain.title: A sustainable quartz supply
chain.desc: Power Growth Accelerators around suitable budding certus quartz. Preserve the budding blocks and leave room for crystal clusters to grow and be harvested.

chain.title: Connect the network
chain.desc: Run Fluix Glass Cable between ME devices. Check channel limits and energy use as you expand; a cable connection alone does not guarantee a device is online.

chain.title: Bring power into ME
chain.desc: Connect a supported external power source to an Energy Acceptor. A small ME network works without a controller, making this a practical place to start.

chain.title: Your first storage cell
chain.desc: Craft a 1k item storage cell. Watch both bytes and distinct item types; many different items can fill the type limit before the byte capacity is exhausted.

chain.title: Give cells a home
chain.desc: Place an ME Drive on the powered network and install a storage cell. Larger cells and additional drives can be added as the collection grows.

chain.title: One window into storage
chain.desc: Connect an ME Terminal to the powered drive network. Deposit and retrieve a test stack, then check device channels if the interface stays offline.

chain.title: Expand beyond the small network
chain.desc: Add an ME Controller when your channel layout needs it. Plan cable routes and device counts before connecting the entire base; the first small storage network does not require one.

chain.title: Craft from stored ingredients
chain.desc: Upgrade to a Crafting Terminal to work directly from network contents. This improves manual crafting without requiring an autocrafting CPU.

chain.title: Describe the recipes
chain.desc: Create a Pattern Encoding Terminal and blank patterns. Encode crafting recipes here, and use processing patterns for external machines with their real input and output amounts.

chain.title: The automatic crafting table
chain.desc: Power and connect a Molecular Assembler beside a Pattern Provider. Assemblers handle encoded crafting recipes; external machines need their own processing setup.

chain.title: Deliver each pattern
chain.desc: Put encoded patterns into a Pattern Provider beside an assembler or machine. Route processing outputs back into ME so requested jobs can finish.

chain.title: A CPU for requested work
chain.desc: Build a small crafting CPU with 1k Crafting Storage and request a test recipe. Increase CPU storage for larger jobs only after the complete input-to-output path works.

chain.title: Storage on the move
chain.desc: Pair a Wireless Terminal with your network using the required wireless infrastructure, then charge it. Range and dimension access depend on the installed wireless system and upgrades.

chain.title: Connect distant ME networks
chain.desc: Plan two complete Quantum Network Bridges and create the entangled singularity pair. This is an optional remote-network project, independent of basic storage and autocrafting.

chain.title: Matter Condensed to a Point
chain.desc: Fit a Matter Condenser with enough storage capacity, select Singularity output, and supply material until a Singularity appears in its output. Keep it for the quantum-network branch or this pack's endgame recipes.
chain.acquisition: Applied Energistics 2 19.2.17 CondenserBlockEntity.getOutput creates the AEItems.SINGULARITY stack for the Singularity output setting. fillOutput and addOutput insert it into the output inventory after the required stored power is reached.

This replaces older list-order and item-count claims.
